subject: Economics
description: Covers structure, Cooperative federalism, 15-year vision, and Atal Innovation Mission.

questions.stem: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on January 1, 2015, replacing the Planning Commission. What is the fundamental philosophical shift in NITI Aayog's approach compared to the Planning Commission?

options.option_text: It acts as a 'think tank' promoting 'cooperative federalism' with a bottom-up approach, unlike the Planning Commission's top-down, centralized resource allocation
It has constitutional authority to dictate economic policies to states, whereas the Planning Commission was merely advisory
It exclusively focuses on private sector privatization, abandoning all social welfare planning
It is entirely controlled by state chief ministers, with the central government having no representation

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Planning Commission followed a "Top-Down" approach (Soviet-style), where a central body in Delhi drafted five-year plans and controlled the allocation of massive funds to states. NITI Aayog has no financial power to allocate funds (that power was returned to the Finance Ministry). Instead, it acts as the premier policy 'Think Tank' of the Government, fostering "Cooperative Federalism" by actively involving State Governments in the policy-making process (bottom-up approach).
DECOY BUSTING: Neither the Planning Commission nor NITI Aayog are constitutional bodies; both were created by executive resolution. It does not dictate policies, it recommends them. The PM remains the chairperson, so the Centre is heavily represented.
EXAM INSIGHT: NITI Aayog fosters "Competitive Federalism" alongside cooperative federalism by releasing various indices (Health Index, Water Management Index, SDG India Index, Export Preparedness Index), forcing states to compete against each other to improve their rankings.

questions.stem: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the NITI Aayog?

options.option_text: The Prime Minister of India
The Union Minister of Finance
The Vice President of India
A prominent economist appointed by the President

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Just like the erstwhile Planning Commission, the Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog. This ensures that the think tank has the highest level of political backing to drive long-term structural reforms across ministries.
DECOY BUSTING: The Finance Minister is a member, not the chair. The Vice President chairs the Rajya Sabha. While economists are appointed as Vice-Chairmen or Members, the PM holds the ultimate chair.
EXAM INSIGHT: Because the PM is busy, the day-to-day operations are run by the Vice-Chairperson (currently Suman Bery) and the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). The Vice-Chairperson holds the rank of a Cabinet Minister.

questions.stem: Which body forms the 'Governing Council' of the NITI Aayog, ensuring the representation of all states?

options.option_text: The Chief Ministers of all States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories
The Finance Ministers of all States
Members of Parliament from the Lok Sabha
Eminent scholars from central universities and IITs

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The defining feature of NITI Aayog that promotes "cooperative federalism" is its Governing Council. It comprises the Prime Minister as its Chairman, along with the Chief Ministers of all States and Union Territories with Legislatures (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K), and Lt. Governors of other UTs. This ensures states have a direct voice in national development agendas.
DECOY BUSTING: The Planning Commission had a similar body called the National Development Council (NDC), but the Planning Commission itself did not have CMs as members. NITI Aayog embeds the states directly into its core Governing Council.
EXAM INSIGHT: There are also "Regional Councils" formed on a need basis to address specific issues impacting more than one state (e.g., a council of Himalayan states).

questions.stem: NITI Aayog has shifted away from Five-Year Plans. Instead, what is the timeframe of the long-term strategic document it formulates?

options.option_text: 15-Year Vision Document, along with a 7-Year Strategy and 3-Year Action Agenda
10-Year Master Plan, reviewed annually
20-Year Centenary Plan aligning with India 2047
Rolling plans that are completely redrafted every single year

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: To break away from the rigid, Soviet-style 5-year planning cycles, NITI Aayog introduced a tiered planning framework. 
- The overarching long-term roadmap is a 15-Year Vision Document (aligning with the UN Sustainable Development Goals timeframe up to 2030).
- This is broken into a 7-Year Strategy Document.
- This is further broken into an operational 3-Year Action Agenda.
DECOY BUSTING: Rolling plans were a concept tried briefly by the Morarji Desai government in the late 1970s. India 2047 is a newer political target, but the formal NITI structure is 15-7-3.
EXAM INSIGHT: This framework allows for much greater flexibility. If a global shock occurs (like a pandemic), the 3-Year Action Agenda can be tweaked without abandoning the 15-Year Vision, whereas 5-Year Plans were notoriously rigid and often failed when economic assumptions changed.

questions.stem: Which flagship initiative was launched by NITI Aayog to foster entrepreneurship and innovation across schools, universities, and industries in India?

options.option_text: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)
Make in India
Startup India
Digital India

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) is the Government of India's flagship initiative, housed within NITI Aayog, to promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship. Its most famous component is the establishment of 'Atal Tinkering Labs' (ATLs) in schools across India to teach students 21st-century skills like 3D printing, robotics, and IoT.
DECOY BUSTING: Make in India, Startup India, and Digital India are massive umbrella programs run by respective ministries (DPIIT under Ministry of Commerce, and MeitY). AIM is specifically the NITI Aayog's brainchild.
EXAM INSIGHT: AIM also sets up Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) in universities to support startups. Questions asking "Which organization runs the Atal Tinkering Labs?" are extremely common in competitive exams.
